changed.change: observeSnapshot now returns a per-observation materializer. Hits capture the frozen exact-payload plan; missing rows return a fresh empty factory; misses eagerly decode/validate/plan then return the fresh decoded graph. loadSnapshot immediately invokes this materializer for unchanged eager paths.

retention.proof: Each root observes each of the three surfaces once. Any hit it captures belongs to the admission-start Map; misses capture decoded graphs rather than an additional plan. Thus captured old plans form a subset of one bounded initial Map. Independent admitted root writers serialize within the store.
retention.release: First successful demand sets materialize to undefined. Unused private captures remain reachable with their root until the scope/context becomes unreachable.

D01.name: warm root Planner skips unrequested Dashboard materialization while cold admission and transactionAll retain validation
D01.oracle: Cold Planner parses all three persisted tagged payloads and their exact total characters. Warm Planner performs zero tagged parses and zero native Dashboard parses. Eager transactionAll performs one native Dashboard parse and parses over 2 MiB more characters. Planner outputs re-encode identically; retained output mutation does not persist; all SQL rows remain unchanged.

observed.name: warm root Planner skips unrequested Dashboard materialization while cold admission and transactionAll retain validation

D02.name: new invalid unrequested SQL payloads reject before root Planner callback on cold and warm stores
D02.oracle: Independent SQL replaces Dashboard and Procurement with malformed JSON, unsupported envelope, invalid shape and negative-version content. Both the warm instance and a new instance reject with the unchanged decoder's error before any Planner callback. Restoring bytes permits the same Planner result; final SQL rows match.

observed.name: new invalid unrequested SQL payloads reject before root Planner callback on cold and warm stores

D03.name: one root materializes a demanded sibling once while nested and current snapshots remain independent staged copies
D03.oracle: Two nested Dashboard reads and two currentSnapshots calls in one Planner root produce exactly one native Dashboard parse. Nested and current outputs are distinct graphs, mutations do not alter siblings or the parent, Planner staged values remain visible, own undefined and -0 survive, and durable rows do not change.

observed.name: one root materializes a demanded sibling once while nested and current snapshots remain independent staged copies

D04.name: ended root scopes reject deferred sibling access before any lazy materialization
D04.oracle: An untouched Dashboard stays unmaterialized during a Planner root. Deferred currentSnapshots and nested Dashboard callbacks reject after root completion, before any JSON.parse or nested callback. The retained Planner snapshot remains an ordinary detached value; later SQL read is unchanged.

observed.name: ended root scopes reject deferred sibling access before any lazy materialization

D05.name: a captured Dashboard plan survives eviction while other surfaces are observed during the same admission
D05.oracle: A reader captures its warm 2 MiB Dashboard plan before changed 2 MiB Planner and Procurement payloads force eviction. Demand after admission yields the original Dashboard bytes via one native Dashboard parse, zero tagged Dashboard parses and exactly two tagged sibling parses, preserving own undefined and -0.

observed.name: a captured Dashboard plan survives eviction while other surfaces are observed during the same admission

D06.name: missing sibling rows invalidate old plans and restore only after a fresh SQL observation
D06.oracle: Deleting the warmed Dashboard SQL row makes nested/current reads inside Planner return isolated empty snapshots. A missing-row output mutation does not become another observation. Re-insertion is observed by the next root, which re-encodes the restored original bytes.

observed.name: missing sibling rows invalidate old plans and restore only after a fresh SQL observation

D07.name: independent writers cannot replace an admitted sibling observation and the next root sees their commit
D07.oracle: An admitted Planner root holds its existing write lock while Dashboard remains undemanded. An independent Dashboard writer cannot enter its callback until release. The first root sees persisted Dashboard, the second commits, and the next first-store Planner root sees the new content/version. This supplements rather than replaces existing same-version CAS tests.

observed.name: independent writers cannot replace an admitted sibling observation and the next root sees their commit

migrationRollback.forwardCompatibility: Existing valid v1 rows are decoded by the unchanged validator on the first observation. Cold stores do not depend on a previous process's memo.
migrationRollback.rollbackOfMission34: Reverting only mission34's local-store.ts optimization to received baseline returns to full decoding and reads the same persisted v1 bytes; no data rewrite or migration is required. This conclusion is scoped to the unchanged snapshot codec and should not be generalized to earlier Finance business-receipt revisions.
migrationRollback.mixedVersionBoundary: New and received-baseline store implementations still use identical SQLite transaction and snapshot formats; the short tests cover independent current-version instances, not a mixed-binary deployment.
migrationRollback.predecessorBoundary: Mission18's compact Finance receipts and all other prior business changes are preserved. Their separate older-reader rollback caveats are not waived by snapshot compatibility.
migrationRollback.performanceOnRollback: Expected loss of the optimization only; no performance-budget guarantee for the old decoder.
